- [ ] 77. Timed challenges (two players, or a daily challenge, 29) need FULLY SEEDED conditions (the owner, 11-Oct). Today the same two seeds (a replay's load and run seeds) give the same level and the same start, but not the same run: a mystery is rolled when it is picked up, from the one stream of dice the whole run shares (traffic, police and hazards draw from it too, as much as the driving makes them), and weighted by the player's social standing; so two players meet different mysteries. Needed: each mystery box (and other pickups' and hazards' chances, and if it is to be fully fair the traffic dealt out) drawing from dice of its own, from the seed and which box it is, so box 3 is the same for everyone whenever it is reached; no standing weighting in a challenge; a challenge code (level, side, car, both seeds) to share; then a friend's replay as the ghost. Changing how mysteries roll changes the rules (version.js logic): every replay and ghost recorded before it stops playing, so better done early.

  - Item 115, owner's answers (12-Oct): blueprints come from a totally separate economy from the game's (money, tips); which one is undecided. The number of ECU levels varies car to car.   - Item 115, replays (owner, 12-Oct): the answer to ECU changes breaking replays is to record the car's stats as they were in the replay itself (so an ECU upgrade, or a rebalance, no longer invalidates it). To work out when built: record the figures the run used in the header (not only `carPrint`), play back with those; keep the car's id, model and perks checks; a ghost needs only the path, so it would not care.
  - Item 115, replays: DECIDE LATER (owner, 12-Oct). Recording only the player's car stats is not enough: everything in the run is driven by figures (traffic kinds, police, rivals, cargo, powerups, gimmicks), so a replay would have to keep the stats of everything in the level. And `cars.js` and the traffic tables are in the replay's `logic` hash (vite.config.js: every `src/delivery/*.js` not on NOT_RULES, with its imports), so any edit to them already refuses every replay, whatever the per-car fingerprint says (read, not tested). Two ways: (1) take the stat tables out of the hash, and have each recording carry a snapshot of every table it used, played back from the snapshot (old replays survive rebalances too; bigger header, bigger change); (2) keep the tables in the hash and record only a small per-car ECU modifier in the header (fixes upgrades, not rebalances; far smaller). Ghosts are unaffected either way (they read only the stored path).
  - Item 115, unlock kinds (owner, 12-Oct; this replaces the earlier "unlocked at ECU0"): ECU0 now means not driveable / locked. Two kinds of car. (1) KEY cars start at ECU1 and blueprints upgrade them, but they are not selectable (not unlocked) until their key is obtained; garage cars are key cars (the key is what they are bought or won with today). (2) BLUEPRINT cars start at ECU0 (locked) and are unlocked on reaching ECU1, so their first X blueprints are the unlock and the car then plays at ECU1. Open: what a key is for a won car (the reward/prize), whether blueprints collected for a key car before its key count, and what "uncompetitive for their tier" now means (it would be ECU1 of a blueprint car).

ADDING A CAR MUST NOT INVALIDATE EVERY REPLAY (the owner, 12-Oct: "invalidating all replays because I added something is really harsh"): `ecus.json` is in the replay `logic` hash (vite.config.js: a file is in the hash unless it is on NOT_RULES), so adding one car's ECU table (item 166 added the Goddess Saloon's and the Fifties Hardtop's) changes the hash and every saved replay is refused. TO DO: stop hashing the whole file. Options, simplest first: (a) a replay records the ECU table entry it ran (its car's stats at its ECU) in its header and plays back from THAT, so the file need not be hashed at all (the replay already records the ECU level); (b) hash only each car's own entry and check the replay's car's entry, so adding or editing another car never refuses it; (c) at least leave added entries out of the hash and hash only the entries that existed. Also check which other data a new car touches that is hashed (cars.js stats are; a new car entry should not change an existing car's replays), and add a check: add a car to the tables and an old replay still plays. Not done; the Goddess/Hardtop promotion (166) refuses old replays until this is fixed.
  - BUILT (16-Oct, branch `claude/replay-stable`, NOT merged, no version bump; tooling and replay metadata only, no game rule changed). FOUND: the fingerprint was sha256 of the WHOLE TEXT of 61 rules files (every src/delivery/*.js not on NOT_RULES plus what they import: cars.js, ecu.js, ecus.json, ideas*.js, levels.js, config.js, tiers.json...), so a car row, an ECU table, a level's import line in levels.js, even a comment, refused every replay. A replay already carried the level's print (its data as loaded) and the car's print (its row), checked on playback. DESIGN (option A/B together): `scripts/logic-hash.mjs` (vite.config.js uses it) hashes the rules as CODE (parsed with Vite's parseAst: comments and layout never count) with each car's own rows and entries left out (in cars.js / ecu.js / ecus.json / ideas*.js: a row with `id: '...'` in a list, bare or in a helper call, and an entry of a table keyed by car ids: KEY_STYLE, KEY_RATING, SUPER_LIVERIES, LEVEL_CARS, DELIVERY, COMPOSURE.bump; never a row with a function in it) and each level's filing left out (levels.js: the `./levels/*.json` imports, the levels in the menu lists, HIDDEN_LEVELS / EVENT_MAPS entries). In return the replay header (`prints: 2`) records at run time what the run reads of them: `figures` (the car's row, its NEW_STATS from the ecu.js tables, its ecus.json row at the ECU driven and at its max, its kind, and the same of its Super version) and `roster` (the garage's CARS in order, each so at its max: traffic drives garage cars at their own top speed and Car Swap lends one, so adding a car to CARS still refuses; adding to the blueprint cars, Bespoke, events, earned, ideas does not). CONFIG, traffic kinds, tables not keyed by car, and all code count as before. Option C (a hand-bumped rules version) rejected: forgettable, and a forgotten bump plays replays wrongly (drift) rather than refusing them. NEW FINGERPRINT on this branch: `27317ec14e` (was `33a7d9d56d` on v1.1.149-alpha, which `BUILD.legacy` still computes the old way). OLD REPLAYS: a header with no `prints` is checked against `BUILD.legacy` (old whole-text hash) plus its level and car prints, so every replay recorded on a build whose rules files are byte-identical still plays (this branch changes no rules file, so all v1.1.149-alpha replays do); as the kept replays are read (replaystore.js, same `delivery_replays` key and layout), each that still plays is given the new prints once and written back, so later car/level additions no longer refuse it. Replays recorded on any older rules stay refused (as today). Once another branch changes a rules file before this merges, the fallback no longer matches and those v1.1.149 replays are the last ones refused by the format change. ReplayStore.kept now replaces a best only if it no longer plays (not merely a different `logic` string).

What was wrong: `nav.js` read back by the depth number in `history.state` alone, and that state outlives the page. After a reload, or a phone that dropped the tab and loaded it again, with a screen open, the old entries were still there with their numbers: the next screen's entry came after them, so back landed on an old entry of the same or a higher number and closed nothing (the Shop or the showroom stayed up), and back from the menu took one or two dead presses before leaving the site. A forward step onto the entry of a screen closed by its own Back did nothing either. Also, the Shop opened from the showroom set `Game.inMenu` false on closing while the showroom was still up (Enter could start a run from it). Fixed: every entry carries its depth AND this load's mark; the menu's entry is taken over when the page loads; back closes the screens above the depth landed on; an earlier load's entries are stepped over, a forward step onto a closed screen is stepped back (`nav.js`); the Shop gives back the `Game.inMenu` it found (`render/shop.js`). New check `scripts/.nav-check.mjs` (a stand-in history: nested screens, own Back buttons, two closed at once, forward steps, reloads, a second round; 24 of its lines fail on the old `nav.js`), in the tiers group. Standard: 136 to 85 layers, tiles 68 to 41 MB scrolled; Car Hunt: 105 to 32 layers, tiles 62 to 34 MB. Branch `claude/showroom-pan`, NOT merged, no version bump (placeholder number: renumber at merge if 217 is taken). CAUSE: the row's ‹ › arrows (and the arrow keys sideways) used the browser's smooth scroll (`row.scrollBy` / `scrollIntoView`, behavior smooth): each tap began a NEW smooth scroll from where the row was, from standing, with the row's proximity snap pulling in between; the row stood still for frames, started again, and taps were lost. FIX: the pan is ours (src/delivery/render/showroompan.js, pure; driven per frame by render/showroom.js): one tap is the same ease-in-out slide as before (smoothstep, 380 ms, onto a column's start: the same end as before for one tap); a tap during a pan moves the TARGET on by a step from the target (not from where the row is) and the slide carries on from where it is at the speed it has (a cubic Hermite, the speed held so it never passes the target and comes back); a tap the other way turns it round smoothly; the snap is off while it moves (class `panning`) and it ends on a column start so nothing is pulled after; a finger, the mouse or the wheel on the row takes over. The arrow keys (sideways rows) go through the same pan; the phone's column and the phone's single-car slide are unchanged. CHECK: scripts/.showroom-check.mjs `rowPan`: on a fake 60 fps clock, 2 / 4 / 8 taps 70 ms apart never move back, never stand still before the end, never return to the start offset, and end exactly N column steps on; one tap is eased in and out; a reversal turns round with no jumping frame; the ends are kept; the old restart-from-standing model stalls (so the check sees it). SEEN (headless Chromium 1194 through the DevTools protocol, 1280x800, sampling `scrollLeft` every frame): 4 taps 120 ms apart, before: ended at 1786 of about 4080 (taps lost), 2 frames standing still mid-pan; after: 4076, 0 standing, 0 px backwards. 6 taps 70 ms apart, before 1531 (2 standing), after 6112 (0). THE PATCH (render/modelpatch.js, pure: extractParts, applyPatch, withSet / withDelete / withAdd / withDuplicate / withMirror): `{ car, version, base, ops: [{id, sig, set}|{id, sig, delete}|{add: {id, kind, params, ...}|{id, from, mirror}}], evil: [{id, sig, set}] }`; ids are child-index paths resolved on the model AS BUILT before any change, a sig (geometry type, vertex count, size; not the place) re-finds a part the code moved; an id that finds nothing is reported as unmatched and skipped (never thrown); a different `base` warns that the code changed. Colours clone the material (never one a traffic copy shares); the paint is re-applied after the model's own livery (userData.livery wrapped). - [x] 257. TRUE SPEED (the owner, 14-Oct: "Lets implement true speed" = real lane lengths on bends; then "Lane changes should scrub some speed as well... part of the agility stat? It still wouldn't be very significant"). Branch `claude/charming-maxwell-pxoail`, NOT merged, no version bump. `CONFIG.trueSpeed` { on, least 0.4, most 2.5, laneScrub 1.2 }; `Track.pathScale(s, lat)` = 1 / (1 - bend x lat), so progress along the road is the distance driven over the length of the car's own line (inside of a bend shorter, outside longer). Applied to the player (`this.s += speed*dt*pathScale`) and to ordinary traffic / racers (traffic.js main advance). Lane changes scrub `laneScrub x across^2 / agility` m/s^2 (across = sideways speed over the car's full sideways speed), never below minSpeed: under 1 m/s for a lane change at 40 m/s, and a nimble car loses less. NOT changed: the screensaver dolly, special traffic states (flyovers, ramps, pursuit), the lap/finish maths (they use s, so a tight inside line is simply faster). REPLAYS: the rules fingerprint changes (player.js / track.js / config.js / traffic.js are inside it), old replays and ghosts are refused (accepted by the owner). CLEAN-RUN TIMES (scripts/level-clocks.mjs --all, flag on vs off; the run keeps the centre of its lane): 34 of 44 timed levels within 0.5%; circuits slower by 3.5-10.6% (grand-prix 222.8 -> 230.6, spa 198.5 -> 207.4, marina-bay 216.9 -> 229.1, montreal 190.1 -> 201.8, stelvio 179.8 -> 191.2, mystery-meadows 98.0 -> 108.4): the clean run drives the lane centre, which on a mostly outside-heavy line is longer. - [x] 262. DAMAGE LOOK AUDITED AND REWORKED (the owner, 14-Oct: "many dents currently look awful"; then, after an 8-car sample, "Go with the ideas and retry the same vehicles"). Branch `claude/damage-audit` (from 9cded11), NOT merged, no version bump. Render-side only (`src/delivery/render/dents.js`, `scripts/.dents-check.mjs`; config and the rules files are untouched). The four stages stay; what changed: (1) parts that are not paint now follow the dents too: small ones (lamps, grilles, mirrors, under 0.35 m) are moved whole by the dents at their centre, larger ones (bumpers, stripes, pinstripes, a roof or cab in a paint of its own, a tarp, a canopy) are bent like the panels. Glass (found by its colour), the wheels and what turns with them (found by render/carsuspension.js), see-through and instanced meshes, and the lamp effects are left alone. (2) The dents are held back: near the glass the paint does not move, so it never goes behind it; nothing gets nearer than 0.6 of its distance to a wheel or the glass; a shove toward the middle stops 0.45 of the way there. The table is now gentle enough that the dents never fold the car through itself (checked numerically: the dent field's Jacobian stays positive). (3) Panels are cut finer once per model, only where the dents bend them (an edge is halved where the dents at its middle differ from the mean of its ends by more than 2 cm, or 5 mm where paint and another part lie together). The cut is kept, and is made on a timer when the car is first seen, not on the first knock. (4) A dent's reach and depth are capped at a big car's size in metres (1.0 / 1.6 / 2.4 m), so a bus is dented at its corners, not along half its length. (5) Stages 1 and 2 were re-authored (a front corner, the tail and a door, then a creased bonnet and a caved door), and the whole table rescaled. Bug fixed on the way: the crumpled copies were computed in the frame the car stood in when first measured, so a car that had driven on was dented in the wrong place. Triangles (the player's car only, at any stage; clean is unchanged): commuter 1764 to 8288, sportscompact 1000 to 10582, junker 2146 to 13158, darkvan 1236 to 10689, city bus 1020 to 2542, lowrider 1984 to 11762, F1 676 to 1524, tuk-tuk 1112 to 3922. Measuring and cutting takes 50 to 300 ms in Node, once per model.

A design = tyre treatment + hub treatment, all rings / discs / bands (rotationally symmetric: reads the same still or turning; no spokes). Six presets: Stock; Whitewall (white ring, 0.64 to 0.88 of the tyre radius, on the outer sidewall); Redline (thin red ring, 0.78 to 0.84); Red tyres, white hubs (rubber recoloured red, hubs white); White hubs on black; Gold hubs, whitewall. Per wheel: a ring is one RingGeometry (16 segments = 32 triangles; one shared geometry per ring shape, one shared material per colour, both flagged shared), 5 mm off the tyre's outer face, a child of the tyre mesh so it rides with the planted wheel; a centre wheel (trike front) gets one each side (64). Colour-only designs add no triangles. Rubber recolour (tyre, tread blocks, sidewall rings) uses per-model clones, never the shared cached materials. THE ORBIT CAMERA for replays and the end of a run (the owner, 15-Oct: "a rotating camera for replays", then: "seamlessly allow the player to orbit the camera from the gameplay cam, and a button to lock it back. Orbit while the replay is playing"). Branch `claude/replay-orbit`, not merged, no version bump. All render-only: `render/orbit.js` (new), `render/orbitdemo.js` (new: a test harness, loaded only by `?orbitdemo=`), and small touches in `render/ghostcar.js`, `render/racewatch.js` (`firstSolid`, `prepareSolids`), `render/road.js` (one flag on the terrain mesh), `render/cargo.js` (the orbit's taps and drags, and O, are not a skip of the delivery), `render/hud.js`, `main.js` (the camera dispatch), `delivery/index.html`, `style.css`, URL-PARAMS.md. NOT `config.js` nor any file in the replay fingerprint (`logicFiles()` run: 66 files, none of the changed ones; the orbit's numbers are in orbit.js, not CONFIG.photo). HOW IT WORKS. IN A REPLAY (playing at 1x/2x/4x, paused or held at its end) a DRAG (mouse button or one finger, past 6 px) on the game view takes hold of the chase camera where it is drawn that frame: yaw, pitch and radius are worked out from the camera's place relative to the car (radius clamped to 15..40 m, pitch to 5..60 degrees) and its aim is kept at where the chase camera looked and eased onto the car over 0.5 s, so the first frame is exactly the chase frame; then the drag turns it. A plain tap or click, a wobble under 6 px, and a wheel or a pinch on the chase camera do nothing. The replay goes on playing while it is orbited (no pause), and a drag-started orbit never turns by itself and keeps the HUD. A small panel bottom right (40 px buttons): Chase view (eases the camera from the orbit pose back to the live chase camera over 0.5 s, position and aim blended, then a new drag starts a new orbit) and Ghost: on/off (default OFF: the best run on the level and side, by the replay's clock, never the very run being watched). The Orbit button in the row (Pause, 1x, Orbit, Exit level) and O start the other kind: it turns by itself (0.22 rad/s) until the player takes hold, again after 4 s alone, with the HUD hidden as photo mode hides it. AT THE END OF A LIVE RUN (the delivery at the kerb, the results): no drag-to-enter (it would fight the tap that skips the delivery); Orbit alone in the row at the top, and Look around on the results (hides them; Results in the panel brings them back). Wheel or pinch zooms inside 15..40 m while orbiting. THE NUDGE: a ray from the car to the camera and two 1.6 m to either side (racewatch `firstSolid`; the terrain by `landAt`: a ray at its mesh took ~40 ms); where blocked the camera is raised, then drawn in; closer than 5 m the usual camera is used that frame. The scenery is boxed once as the orbit comes on offer so a look costs under ~1.5 ms every 0.1 s (headless). Left-hand levels go through `aim()`; Photo mode is untouched. SEEN, 15-Oct, in a REAL REPLAY driven headless (`?orbitdemo=` records a ghost-driven run A to its delivery, a slower run B, then plays B back with Replay.watch; stills with scripts/shots.mjs, /tmp/replaycam-investigation/o2/): the chase view mid-replay with the REPLAY badge and the row Pause / 1x / Orbit / Exit level; a synthetic mouse drag entering the orbit: the pose in the car's own terms (m ahead, m to the side, m up, look direction, fov) on the last chase frame was [-14, 0.61, 9.9, 0.923, 0, -0.385, 76.798] and on the first orbit frame [-14, 0.61, 9.9, 0.923, 0, -0.385, 76.798] (the same to three decimals; six steps later); the drag then swung it 88.7 degrees round (yaw 176.9 to 88.2) while the replay clock went on (steps 908 to 926, 7.57 s to 7.72 s, not paused), auto-spin off; the way back held at 0.15, 0.5 and 0.85 of the blend (the camera pose moved [0.5, 14.0, 9.9] to [-1.7, 11.9] to [-6.8, 7.1] to [-11.8, 2.4] to the chase [-14, 0.2, 9.9], the look direction ahead 0 to 0.20 to 0.63 to 0.89 to 0.92, stills lock_015 / lock_05 / lock_085); a tap, a wobble and a wheel on the chase camera did nothing; the Ghost button in the panel turning the replay ghost on (the line under the clock saying 'Ghost 46 m ahead', now put under the REPLAY badge instead of behind it); a 390x844 phone still of the replay orbited (HUD whole, top row Pause / 1x / Exit level, the panel bottom right). TRACED (render/showroom.js `goTo` -> `pick` -> `showDetail`, render/showroomview.js `show`): the whole detail is rebuilt (`detail.replaceChildren`, new `.sr-dpic`); `ShowroomView.show()` drops the old model, builds the new one, moves the one 2D canvas into the new picture, and the first draw was left to the NEXT animation frame, drawn at fade alpha 0 (`bounceOffset` alpha 0 at t=0, 0.25 s fade-in). REPRODUCED (headless Chromium over the DevTools protocol, touch emulation, 1280x800 at ratio 3, ArrowRight x3, a per-frame log of the live canvas's alpha): the first painted frame after every switch had the NEW words and an EMPTY canvas (alpha sum 0), then the car faded up over the next frames (software GL, so stalls of 100 to 630 ms stretched it): old car gone in one frame, blank stage, new car fading in = a blink. CAUSE (certain for the blank frame; that it is THE flicker the owner sees on the tablet is likely, not seen on it): the first frame's shader compile and texture upload ran in a frame whose result is painted blank. FIX (render-only, replays unaffected): on a switch (another car after one was on screen) `show()` draws the new car's first frame at once, in the same task as the new words (so the compile stall happens before the browser paints and the old picture stays up until the new car is in the canvas), and that switch skips the alpha fade (the car still drops and bounces); the first opening of the showroom and reduced motion keep the fade; `draw` split into `draw`/`frameAt`, dt kept non-negative. (3) BLOCKED WHEELS, "depends how blocked": the all-or-nothing ray rule is replaced (render/rims.js roomFor). Per face, 36 rays along the axle measure `clear` (share meeting nothing) and `depth` (how far off the tyre the nearest bodywork is). The rim goes BEHIND what covers it, as a real wheel sits behind its arch: WHOLE if it fits (depth >= 61.5 mm), else a FLAT variant of the same design (no dish, lip and spokes side by side in one plane, spokes' backs sunk into the tyre, cap 4.5 mm over: 9.5 mm deep, 5 mm off the tyre, needs depth >= 19 mm; a design's sidewall ring gives way on that face). A face wears a rim if clear >= 0.9 (whole; a mudguard edge or bracket over a sliver is let be) or clear >= 0.4 and it fits behind; else stock. Inner twin tyres (face against the outer tyre) are left out. Then PER AXLE (tyres within r/3 along the car): the worse face decides, so an axle never mixes rim and stock, unless lopsided (one face >= 0.97 open, the other < 0.05), and an axle is all whole or all flat. Thresholds tuned by looking (the owner's 0.6-0.7 left every half-mudguarded classic stock; at 0.4 + fit-behind they look right). Result: 190 of 220 cars wear rims (was 182); no rims at all: bug (bodywork 1-8 mm off the wheels), sidecar (5-15 mm), ufo, earned-ufo; mixed by axle: tuk-tuk (front centre wheel stock, 15 mm), snake / super-snake (rear stock, 8 mm), tinsnail (rear stock, 2 mm), swancar (rear stock), rallywedge (rear stock, 7 mm). Flat rims under mudguards: bubble, keiroadster, teardrop, flyingcar, dragster (middle), solarracer, tipper / mixer / wrecker fronts, dunebuggy, armoured, bathtub, gyrocar, mower, duckwagon, cabledrum, gameviewer. (1) RECORDED AT BUILD (render/shapeedits.js): inside a car's own model build (carShapes in showcar.js, items.js, ideaslot.js) three.js's Shape.extractPoints (extrusions, flat shapes) and a lathe's profile are hooked; each outline gets an id from its own points (`s<hash>#<n>`), its points in its own plane, depth / bevel, and the geometry made; locateShapes finds it on the car (its mesh, or its vertex run inside a merged mesh, also moved / turned copies) and the matrix from its plane to the model. Outside a scope with edits or recording nothing is hooked (the plain game never installs the hooks). The model files' geometry caches (16 of them) make a fresh copy while a scope is live, so the plain cars' cache is never touched. (2) THE EDIT IS A BUILD INPUT: the patch's `shapes` table `{ id: [[u, v], ...] }` is read as the outline is extruded (the same helper, bevel, merge, materials, draw calls); a stale id is reported. On a phone the view's extra toggles step aside while a shape is open (views, Snap, Mirror stay). In the Part tab, the precise route: big numbered handles in a 2D view that matches the screen (side / top / front; flips with the camera), the original dashed, the car's other shapes faint; the numbers and outline are drawn on the car too (the picked point orange and larger); drag, type, + (point after), x (remove), Zoom in (4x on the picked point), Reset shape. It is a burst main's water with no main, there all the time: `Track.icy` gives it `{ water: true }`, so the player brakes, steers and changes lane by CONFIG.waterMain's numbers, and the tyres stay wet over the `wetAfter` tail. It got its own key rather than an option on `waterMains`, because a main is a point with a lane, a fountain and a cycle, while a patch is a stretch with or without a lane. NEW KEY `wetness: { strength, tail }` sets how slippery water is on the level's surface. It covers burst mains, standing water and the wet tail after either, but NOT the tide, fords or water stages, which have numbers of their own (CONFIG.tide.steerGrip, Water.feel) and were not touched. track.js `waterNumbers(level)` / `Track.wet` is the one place the numbers come from; player.js reads only that. Each share of grip loses strength times its loss at 1, with a floor (CONFIG.waterMain.floor: brakes 0.2, steering 0.15, lane speed 0.3), and wetAfter is multiplied by tail. With no key, or 1 and 1, the numbers are CONFIG.waterMain's exactly; with strength 0, water is not slippery at all. The schema has bounds of 0-3 and 0.1-5, and there is help text in the editor. Branch `claude/lane-scrub` from main fbc1d57 (v1.1.148-alpha), NOT merged, no version bump. WHY: the old scrub (257: `laneScrub` 1.2 m/s^2 x across^2 / agility) is undone by the engine's pull: with the accelerator held a lane change at top speed cost 0.02 m/s. NEW `CONFIG.trueSpeed.driven` { cancel 1, lose 4, most 6, from 0.8, full 0.95, least 0.05, tune 1 } (config.js, with the docs), applied in player.js `update` (the lane scrub block) from what `updateSpeed` records (`pulling`: the m/s^2 the engine pulled this step with the accelerator held; `speedTop`: the top speed this step). With the accelerator held, at full sideways speed (across^2 as before) the scrub takes back the engine's pull (cancel 1: the pedal does nothing mid-change) plus lose / agility m/s^2 (capped at most 6). That is weighed by how near top speed the car was as the steer went on (a smoothstep from 0.8 to 0.95 of top), kept while the steer is held, never under least 0.05: a car starting the change at top speed is scrubbed all through it, and a car still climbing gets only a twentieth. Off the accelerator (hands off: the speed holds; braking) only the old laneScrub acts, the same to the bit. Top speed is never touched: going straight, every car reaches its top exactly and holds it. Not applied under a turbo or a boost pad (scrubbed as before), pulling away after a drop (`launching`), afloat, or to traffic and racers (traffic.js has no lane scrub; unchanged). The tank, a flat tyre, bad gas / the weight and ice / water are included through the pull they actually have (on ice the pull and the across are both smaller, so the extra is smaller). Never below CONFIG.minSpeed (as before). MEASURED (`node scripts/.lanescrub-check.mjs --table`, stock ECU, a straight on a stripped Gimmick Road 2; behind = metres behind a ghost that drove straight from the same start with the same pedal, at 6 s).
